headline: FFO grows on leasing gains despite a tough prior-year comp
summary_short: Vornado's Q2 2026 revenue was $462.2M (+4.7% y/y), and FFO as adjusted rose 19.6% y/y to $0.67/diluted share, while GAAP net income attributable to Vornado of $32.0M was down sharply from $759.3M a year earlier, a period that included an $803.2M gain on the 770 Broadway NYU master lease.
summary_long: Revenue rose 4.7% y/y and 0.7% q/q to $462.2M. FFO as adjusted was $131.1M ($0.67/share, +19.6% y/y) on rent commencements (+$13.3M), a smaller NYU lease drag (+$8.9M) and higher signage revenue (+$8.0M), partly offset by higher 2033-notes interest expense (-$10.2M). Same-store NOI at share rose 9.8% y/y. GAAP net income attributable to Vornado fell to $32.0M from $759.3M a year ago, mainly reflecting the loss of an $803.2M one-time gain on the 770 Broadway NYU master lease booked in Q2 2025. Cash fell to $675.4M; shareholders' equity was $5,787.6M, down 5.0% y/y, partly on $53.5M of Q2 share repurchases. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Q2 2025 included an $803.2M gain on the 770 Broadway master lease with NYU; Q2 2026 had no comparable gain, driving the y/y decline.
Same-store NOI at share rose 9.8% y/y, led by New York office/retail (+11.9%) and THE MART (+9.1%), partly offset by 555 California Street (-14.3%).
Y/y increase reflects a new $500M 5.75% senior notes offering (Jan 2026) and an upsized term loan, partly offset by repayment of $400M notes at their June 2026 maturity.
Release discloses $53.5M of Q2 common share repurchases (1,787,090 shares); no full equity roll-forward is given, so the decline is only partly explained.
FFO, as adjusted, rose 19.6% y/y on rent commencements (+$13.3M), a smaller NYU lease drag (+$8.9M) and higher signage revenue (+$8.0M), partly offset by higher 2033-notes interest expense (-$10.2M).
